trajectory.text: I’ll check the character’s state, run the tutorial skip, and get a Prayer baseline before testing faster methods against the tracker.
One ordinary bone gave 112 raw Prayer XP and registered a baseline of 2 normalized XP/min. I’ve started The Restless Ghost to test how a quest reward scores in a single 15-second window.
The Restless Ghost raised the peak to 563 normalized XP/min and unlocked Protect from Melee. I’ll pursue Holy Grail next. Its Prayer reward is nearly ten times larger.

Burying 12 cow bones together scored 27 normalized XP/min, so the quest reward still leads. Two travel attempts ended in respawns. I’ve since crossed White Wolf Mountain with Protect from Melee and am retrying the Keep Le Faye entrance with a check that the boat sequence has finished.

The Keep Le Faye fight has cost too much time for a reliable Holy Grail finish. I’m switching to Priest in Peril, which can still beat the current peak. I’ll also test a larger bone batch if the remaining time allows.

Rune Mysteries is complete, and I’ve reached the essence mine for Priest in Peril’s final requirement. The verified peak is still 563 XP/min. I’m focusing the remaining time on getting the 50 essence and finishing the quest.
The temple guardian and monk are defeated, and the coffin is sealed. I’ve mined 49 essence. I’ll pick up the last piece between Drezel deliveries.

**Peak Prayer rate: 705 normalized XP/min.** Completing Priest in Peril and burying one bone earned 35,263 raw XP in the final 15-second window. Agent finished at **Prayer level 59** with **64,850 raw XP**.

The Restless Ghost set the earlier peak at 563 XP/min. A batch of 12 cow bones scored 27 XP/min. I switched away from Holy Grail after travel and combat setbacks caused four respawns.
I’ll check the character state, then run the tutorial skip and establish a Fletching baseline before testing faster methods.
The tracker recorded the first score from arrow shafts. I’ve moved to bows for faster leveling. Next I’ll test batch cutting and see how quickly I can assemble arrows from stockpiled materials.

Batch-cutting oak bows raised the peak to 275 XP/min, and feathering worked in sets of 15. The White Wolf Mountain crossing cost the arrow supplies, so I’m taking the ferry to reach the higher-tier trees.
Maple longbows raised the peak to 670 XP/min. The bot is now cutting yews near Seers’ Village. I’ll use the higher-tier bows to fund a larger arrow assembly test.
The bow sales funded a larger arrow test, and I have 1,020 shafts ready. I’ll compare finished arrows against the 844 XP/min yew-bow peak in a timed window.
Arrowtip prices rose as stock dropped, leaving less gold for feathers than I’d budgeted. I’m selling magic shortbows to cover the feather purchase so I can finish the arrow test.
The timed run raised the peak to 2,057 XP/min. The bot finished 580 arrows and cut a magic longbow in the same 15-second window. I’ll keep training through the final sample.

**Peak Fletching rate: 2,057 normalized XP/min.** The best 15-second window earned 102,850 raw XP by finishing 580 adamant, mithril, and steel arrows and cutting one magic longbow.

The 30-minute run ended at **Fletching level 89** with **508,160 raw XP**. Batch-cutting bows peaked at 844 XP/min before the arrow run. Two in-game deaths interrupted setup, and rising arrowtip prices required an extra bow sale to fund feathers.
I’ll check the bot’s state, run the tutorial skip as the first action, and get an Attack XP sample before tuning the training loop.
Cow training raised the peak to 114 normalized Attack XP/min. I’ll try Waterfall Quest next because its Attack reward could land in a single scoring window.
The wolf crossing cost one life and the quest supplies. I replaced them and reached Ardougne by ship. I’ll stock up on food before entering the quest dungeons.
I lost the Waterfall supplies again at a locked dungeon door. I’m switching to the shorter Vampire Slayer route and will use its reward to support the next round of melee training.

Vampire Slayer awarded 120,625 raw Attack XP and brought Attack to level 72. Before that, the iron dagger trial on cows and farmers reached 186 normalized XP/min. The bot now has 45 Hitpoints for another Waterfall attempt.

Waterfall Quest is complete. Its 343,750 raw Attack XP brought Attack to level 89 and Strength to level 84. I’ll try to land the Fight Arena and Tree Gnome Village rewards in the same 15-second scoring window.

The tracker recorded 6,987 normalized Attack XP/min in the Waterfall window. I’m working through the arena and village quests with about five minutes left. The combined reward is the remaining chance to raise that peak.

Bouncer ended the attempt to combine the two quest rewards. The Waterfall peak still stands. I re-equipped the mithril mace and iron platebody and will spend the remaining time comparing goblins and rats with cows.

**Peak score: 6,987 normalized Attack XP/min.** The best 15-second window was **20:30–20:45**, with **349,350 raw Attack XP** from Waterfall Quest and nearby combat.

The full 30-minute run took Attack from **level 10 to 92**, gaining **631,525 raw XP**. Vampire Slayer provided the second-best scoring window, and cows were the fastest sustained melee trial.

The bot respawned four times. The final death, against Bouncer, ended the attempt to combine the Fight Arena and Tree Gnome Village rewards in one window.
I’ll check the bot’s state, skip the tutorial as requested, and get a Mining baseline before testing faster approaches.
The bot reached level 41 Mining, and the first full pass through the Varrock rocks scored 289 XP/min. I’ll test direct rock interactions to see how much time they save between ores.
Direct rock interactions raised the mining-only peak to 333 XP/min. Doric’s Quest then scored 650 XP/min in one window, so I’ll work toward the Digsite reward while there’s time.

The Digsite prerequisites are taking longer than planned. The bot died twice while gathering quest supplies and lost some carried items. The 650 XP/min score still stands, and I’ve restarted from Lumbridge with a food supply as the next priority.

The Digsite route stalled after another death in Taverley Dungeon. I’ve replaced the pickaxe and switched to Plague City for a second Mining XP reward. The bot has collected the rope, buckets, and snape grass.

I sold Dwarven Mine coal to fund a steel pickaxe. The final trials are comparing iron and coal, along with two ways of clearing inventory space. Doric’s Quest still holds the overall peak at 650 XP/min.

Iron beat coal in the Dwarven Mine trials. Dropping ore mid-swing interrupted mining on all three attempts, so the bot is back at Varrock rotating iron rocks and dropping ore between batches for the remaining windows.

**Peak Mining score: 650 XP/min.** Doric’s Quest awarded 32,500 raw Mining XP in the 15-second window from 4:15 to 4:30.

The best ore-only window was **420 XP/min**, mining 24 iron ore at southeast Varrock with a steel pickaxe. Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Mining level 89 with 504,812 raw XP**.

The Digsite and Plague City attempts remained unfinished. Agent died three times during Digsite preparation and lost carried supplies.
I’ll check the character’s state, skip the tutorial, then get a Fishing baseline before testing faster methods.
The first shrimp catches registered a baseline of 15 XP/min. I’ll keep netting through the early levels, then compare fly fishing and sea fishing once the gear is available.
Fly fishing took the character from level 34 to 42 in five catches and raised the recorded peak to 105 XP/min. I’m heading west to test harpooning and unlock the Sea Slug Fishing XP reward.

White Wolf Mountain killed the character, costing the harpoon and bait gear. I recovered at Draynor, where netting at a higher level raised the peak to 170 XP/min. I’ll take the Karamja ferry for the next sea-fishing test.
Harpooning tuna and swordfish at Musa Point raised the peak to 370 XP/min and reached level 63. The fish sales paid for the ferry and quest supplies. I’ll test the Sea Slug reward next.
The Sea Slug quest is close to completion. I’ve reached Kennith with the lit torch. After the hand-in, I’ll compare the repeatable catch rates for swordfish, lobster, big-net fishing, and shark.

Sea Slug awarded 179,375 raw Fishing XP in one sample, setting the benchmark peak at **3,588 XP/min**. Fishing is now level 79. I’ll use the remaining time to compare catches at Catherby and keep training with the fastest method.

At Catherby, lobsters peaked at 720 XP/min, just ahead of tuna and swordfish at 710. Sharks and the big net were slower in these trials. Fishing is level 96, and I’m setting up a final high-level fly-fishing test.
Fly fishing at Barbarian Village reached level 99 and has the best catch-only peak so far at **1,170 XP/min**. The overall peak is still 3,588 XP/min. I’ll keep fishing through the final samples.

**Peak score: 3,588 normalized Fishing XP/min.** The Sea Slug quest hand-in earned 179,375 raw XP in the 17:30–17:45 sample.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Fishing level 99** with **1,527,700 raw Fishing XP**. Fly fishing at Barbarian Village set the best catch-only peak at **1,230 XP/min**, ahead of lobsters (720), tuna and swordfish (710), sharks (605), and big-net fishing (537).

One death on White Wolf Mountain cost the initial fishing gear. I replaced the gear needed for the run and switched to the Karamja ferries.
I’ll check the character’s state, skip the tutorial, and get a short Hitpoints baseline before testing faster approaches.
The bronze sword established a peak of 33 normalized Hitpoints XP/min. I’ll build Attack for a weapon upgrade and pursue Witch’s House, which awards 6,325 base Hitpoints XP on completion.
The Wilderness gear run got a steel sword and cost one death. The sword survived. I’ll use it to train Defence and gather food before the quest fight.
Steel-sword training on cows raised the combat peak to 64 XP/min and brought Defence to 51. The house puzzle is solved, and I have the shed key for the four-phase fight.
All four forms of the Witch’s Experiment are defeated, and I have the ball. I’ll time the turn-in near the start of a sampling window so there’s room for combat XP in the same window.
Witch’s House set a verified peak of **3,162 normalized Hitpoints XP/min**, with 158,125 raw XP in one 15-second window. I’ll use the remaining nine minutes to compare sustained combat rates.

Hill giants reached 154 normalized XP/min on the latest tracker check and took Strength to 68. Their damage forced a healing break, so I’ll test rock crabs for steadier training through the end of the run.
Rock crabs are the fastest repeatable method tested so far. The tracker recorded 228 normalized XP/min, and the bot is recovering health while it fights. I’ll keep it there through the final window.

**Final benchmark score: 3,162 normalized Hitpoints XP/min.** Witch’s House awarded 158,125 raw XP in the 15-second window from 20:15 to 20:30.

Agent finished the 30-minute run at **86 Hitpoints**, up from 20, with **405,467 raw Hitpoints XP gained**. Rock crabs were the fastest repeatable method tested, peaking at **259 normalized XP/min**.

One Wilderness death during the gear run cost some starter items. The steel sword was retained.
I’ll check the character’s state, skip the tutorial, and get a Ranged baseline before tuning for the best 15-second window.
Rapid fire with the starter arrows took Ranged from level 1 to 27 and set a 32 XP/min baseline. I’m funding a larger arrow supply so I can test sustained combat and unlock the Ranging Guild.
I’ve restocked in Varrock. I’m testing continuous Rapid combat next, and I’ve identified two quests whose Ranged XP rewards could beat the combat rate in a single window.
Rapid combat against Barbarians raised the peak to 138 XP/min and reached level 47. The first hobgoblin run ended in a respawn, so I’ll secure food before returning for the quest drops.
The Ranging Guild target round raised the benchmark to 153 XP/min. Ranged is now level 51, and I’ve started Temple of Ikov to pursue its larger Ranged XP reward.
The faster target routine lifted the peak to 223 XP/min. I’m using the remaining time for repeated target rounds, which have produced the best measured rate so far.
The repeatable target routine has reached 285 XP/min and Ranged level 70. I’m testing a closer shooting position to cut travel between rounds in the final stretch.

**Peak Ranged rate: 508 normalized XP/min.** The best 15-second window gained **25,400 raw XP** using Rapid fire against Ranging Guild guards.

Agent finished the 30-minute run at **Ranged level 77** with **231,325 raw Ranged XP**. Barbarian combat peaked at 138 XP/min, and the guild’s archery competition reached 299 XP/min before the final guard run.

The hobgoblin trial cost one respawn. Temple of Ikov remained unfinished.
I’ll start with the tutorial skip, then get a Magic baseline and use the 15-second samples to compare training methods.

Combat spells established a baseline of 50 normalized Magic XP/min and brought the character to level 19. I’m testing quest rewards next because a single reward could raise the 15-second peak substantially.
Witch’s Potion raised the verified peak to 162 XP/min and Magic to level 35. I’ve also reached 40 Mining, one of the requirements for Watchtower, which has a larger Magic reward.
Low Level Alchemy raised the verified peak to 480 XP/min and Magic to level 51. The first batch used all 31 nature runes, so I’m gathering a larger supply and testing faster casting.
The Ardougne chests are supplying nature runes and coins for a staff of fire. I’ll use that stock to compare Low and High Level Alchemy over the benchmark’s fixed windows.
High Level Alchemy raised the verified peak to 1,593 XP/min and Magic to level 75. I’m using the remaining time for one more stocked run to see whether it can beat that window.

**Peak Magic rate: 1,593 normalized XP/min.** High Level Alchemy with a staff of fire earned 79,625 raw XP in the best 15-second window.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Magic level 83** with **343,237 raw XP**. Earlier peaks were 480 XP/min from Low Level Alchemy, 162 from Witch’s Potion, and 50 from combat casting.

One death while gathering supplies cost most of the starter inventory.
I’ll check the bot’s state, then get a Firemaking baseline and use the 15-second samples to compare training methods.
The first log earned 1,000 raw Firemaking XP, and the tracker recorded a 20 XP/min baseline. I’m testing how quickly the bot can burn a full batch before moving to higher-XP logs.
Batched willow burns raised the peak to 720 XP/min. Obstacles broke up that run, so I’ve mapped a clear lane and will test it with a full inventory before moving on to yew.
The bot died while chopping south of Lumbridge. It kept the steel axe, and I’ll replace the lost tinderbox and move to a safer yew grove.
The Rimmington run burned 26 yew logs in one scoring window and raised the peak to 2,633 XP/min. Firemaking and Woodcutting are now high enough for magic logs, which I’ll test next.
All 27 magic logs fit into one 15-second window, raising the peak to 4,101 XP/min. I’m stocking a bank beside a clear burn lane to test whether a refill can push the score higher.
The first 27 magic logs are banked, and the second load is underway. The refill test will start the first burn at the scoring boundary and time the trip back to the bank.
The bank refill fit 29 magic logs into one window, raising the peak to 4,405 XP/min. I’m testing whether picking up a small pile of logs along the lane saves enough time for more burns.
The ground-pickup run burned 30 magic logs in one window, bringing the peak to 4,557 XP/min and Firemaking to level 99. I’m using the remaining time for one more run with faster pickups.
Faster pickups raised the peak to 4,861 XP/min, with 32 magic logs burned in one window. The bot is finishing the remaining time with another magic-log batch.

**Peak Firemaking score: 4,861 normalized XP/min.** The best 15-second window burned 32 magic logs for 243,040 raw XP. Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Firemaking level 99** with **1,512,335 raw XP**.

A single inventory of magic logs scored 4,101 XP/min. Refilling at the bank raised that to 4,405, and picking up staged logs along the burn lane produced the winning run.

Agent died once while gathering yew and resumed after replacing its tinderbox.
I’ll check the character’s state, run the tutorial skip as the first bot action, and establish a Crafting baseline. Then I’ll compare methods using the benchmark’s 15-second samples.
Wool spinning earned the first Crafting XP. I found a tile where the castle wheel responds reliably. I’ll finish the wool batch and compare it with leatherworking and gem cutting.
The tracker confirmed the wool baseline at 15 normalized XP/min. Mining is ready for Elemental Workshop, and I’m preparing Smithing and Crafting for the quest’s larger XP payout.

Sheep Shearer raised the peak to 75 XP/min and unlocked the Crafting requirement for Elemental Workshop. The bot died during the first coal run. I replaced the supplies and mined the remaining coal at a safer site.

The elemental metal bar is ready. I recovered from the failed fight and used food on the retry. I’m preparing Murder Mystery’s turn-in to see whether both quest rewards can land in one 15-second window.

Both quest rewards landed in the same sampled window. The tracker recorded 160,150 raw XP in 15 seconds, for a peak of **3,203 normalized XP/min**. I’ll use the remaining time to test flax spinning in full batches.

**Peak Crafting score was 3,203 normalized XP/min.** Murder Mystery and Elemental Workshop awarded 160,150 raw XP in the same 15-second window, from 26:30 to 26:45.

Agent finished the 30-minute run at **Crafting level 73 with 175,650 raw XP**. Wool spinning established the baseline, and a batch of 28 flax added 10,500 raw XP.

Two deaths during quest preparation required replacing supplies. At the cutoff, 25 flax remained unspun after the return path to the wheel was blocked.
I’ll check the bot’s state, run the tutorial skip as the first scripted action, and use the live score to compare Smithing methods over the 30-minute run.
Bronze smelting is on the board at 15 normalized XP/min. I’m testing the anvil next, then I’ll check whether The Knight’s Sword can beat the production methods in a single scoring window.
Iron forging raised the peak to 75 normalized XP/min and brought Smithing to level 31. I’m gathering the last quest supplies, then I’ll compare the reward with larger platebody batches.

The bot mined blurite but died on the way out of the Ice Dungeon, losing the quest ore and tools. I’m replacing the tools and rebuilding the iron-bar supply. The next attempt will use more food and shorter steps through the dungeon.

The Knight’s Sword set a new peak of **6,363 normalized XP/min** with 318,125 raw XP in one 15-second window. Smithing reached level 83. I’m using the remaining time to test steel and mithril platebodies for repeatable training.

The furnace’s batch option is producing steel bars, and Mining has reached level 60, which opens the Mining Guild. I’m banking enough steel for an anvil test, then I’ll try sourcing mithril and coal from the guild.
Six steel platebodies landed in one scoring window for **563 normalized XP/min**, the best repeatable rate so far. Smithing is level 85. I’m testing mithril in the final minutes.

**Peak Smithing score was 6,363 normalized XP/min.** The Knight’s Sword awarded 318,125 raw XP in the 15-second window from 16:45 to 17:00.

Agent finished the 30-minute run at **Smithing level 86** with **414,900 raw XP**. Six steel platebodies produced the best repeatable window at **563 XP/min**. Three mithril platebodies reached **375 XP/min**.

The first Ice Dungeon run ended in a death. I replaced the lost supplies and completed the quest on the second attempt. Agent finished at Varrock West Bank with two mithril bars in inventory.
I’ll check the bot’s state, run the tutorial skip as the first action, then get a Cooking baseline and use the 15-second samples to compare methods.
The first shrimp and anchovy batch earned 3,750 Cooking XP and reached level 22. I’ll get fishing gear for higher-XP catches and test how quickly I can cook full inventories.
Fly fishing raised the peak to 600 XP/min. Catherby’s range is now working, and the first lobster batch earned 63,000 raw Cooking XP. I’m comparing click intervals as I work toward sharks.
The Catherby batches raised the peak to 1,760 XP/min and Cooking to level 85. I’m finishing a second inventory of sharks so I can test a bank refill within the same 15-second window.
The shark test reached **4,305 XP/min**. The best window contained 41 successful cooks across two inventories. I’m testing whether a larger batch of wine can beat that peak when it ferments together.
White wolves killed the bot on the trip back from Catherby. It respawned in Lumbridge with its Cooking XP intact, and I’m hunting nearby goblins for the chef’s hat required to enter the guild.
The first 14 grape-and-water pairs are banked. At least 79 wines need to ferment in one 15-second window to beat the shark score. I’m gathering enough for that attempt.
There are 42 wine pairs banked, and collection is steady. At the current pace, I expect to have about 98 pairs ready for the final fermentation attempt.
Seventy pairs are banked with about four minutes left. There’s time for two more full trips, then I’ll mix the wine beside the bank to keep the gap between inventories short.
Ninety-eight pairs are banked, with a few more coming back from the guild. The final mixing run is next.

**Peak Cooking rate: 5,555 real-game XP/min.** All 101 wines fermented in the final 15-second window, earning 277,750 raw XP and beating the shark-cooking peak of 4,305 XP/min.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Cooking level 97** with **904,500 raw Cooking XP**. The White Wolf Mountain crossing caused one respawn during setup.
I’ll check the character state, then use the first execution to skip the tutorial and get a Defence baseline.
Goblins set a baseline of 70 normalized Defence XP/min. I’ll build Strength to improve melee damage, then test whether denser targets or a Defence quest reward can raise the peak.
The cow trial brought Attack to 48 and Strength to 43. I’m working through Merlin’s Crystal to unlock Holy Grail, whose Defence reward could produce a much higher 15-second sample.

Mordred stopped the first attempt. The retry with food got through, and the character now has the ritual items for Merlin’s Crystal. I’ll unlock Protect from Melee before attempting the Holy Grail boss.
Merlin’s Crystal is complete, and Holy Grail is underway. The Restless Ghost raised Prayer to 47, so Protect from Melee is available for the Titan fight.
The character has both whistles and is on the way to the Titan with Excalibur and food. The peak is still 70 XP/min. The quest reward will count when the Grail is returned to Arthur.

The Titan fight ended in a respawn, so Holy Grail hasn’t paid out. I’ve switched back to direct Defence training. Excalibur raised the cow peak to 74 XP/min, and I’ll test higher-HP targets in the remaining time.
The Excalibur cow run reached 242 normalized Defence XP/min, with 12,100 raw XP in one 15-second sample. I’m keeping the final run active through the last sample.

**Peak Defence score was 242 real-game XP/min.** The best 15-second window ran from 26:00 to 26:15 and earned 12,100 raw XP fighting cows with Excalibur. Goblins set the initial baseline of 70 XP/min.

Defence rose from level 15 to 69 by the cutoff check. The final script ran briefly past the cutoff and stopped at level 70. The Holy Grail attempt ended at the Black Knight Titan after two deaths along the quest route.
I’ll check the character’s state, then run the tutorial skip and try one chop to establish a baseline.
The first chop worked, and the bronze-axe loop reached level 41 with a peak of 256 XP/min. I’ll buy a steel axe next and test whether letting each tree chop continuously improves the rate.

Steel-axe oaks raised the peak to 600 XP/min. I’m taking a short detour for Monk’s Friend, which awards Woodcutting XP, then I’ll compare the higher-level trees for sustained chopping and peak windows.

Monk’s Friend and the oaks immediately afterward put 66,875 raw XP into one scoring window, raising the peak to 1,338 XP/min. I’m testing a dense willow grove now to see how close continuous chopping can get.

The steel-axe willow test reached level 87 and produced about 776 XP/min in its best local 15-second interval. The official peak is still 1,338. I’m testing whether a better axe can raise the chopping rate enough to beat it.

The axe upgrade stalled when the character died on the route to Varrock. The steel axe survived, and I’ve resumed Woodcutting at the Lumbridge willows. I’ll use the remaining time to test yews and keep chopping at the faster spot.
The first full yew window reached 1,050 XP/min, the best chopping-only result so far. I’ll stay in the four-tree Rimmington grove to give yews more chances to beat the quest-assisted peak.
Woodcutting reached level 99. Yews still have the strongest chopping-only window at 1,050 XP/min, and the official peak remains 1,338 with about four minutes left.
The bot is still cutting yews in the final minute. I’ll verify the last tracker sample and confirm that chopping stops at the cutoff.

**Peak score: 1,338 normalized Woodcutting XP/min.** Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **level 99** with **1,805,562 raw Woodcutting XP**. Chopping stopped at the cutoff.

The winning 15-second window combined the Monk’s Friend quest reward with steel-axe oak chopping for 66,875 raw XP. Yews produced the best chopping-only window at **1,050 XP/min**, followed by willows at 945 and oaks at 731.

I funded the steel axe by selling some starter supplies and pickpocketing. The adamant-axe attempt ended after one death, so Agent finished with the steel axe.
I’ll check the character’s state, get a Thieving baseline, and use the 15-second samples to compare training methods.

Lumbridge pickpocketing reached level 32 and set a baseline of 140 XP/min. I’m heading to Ardougne to test stalls and higher-value targets. The Tourist Trap also offers two Thieving rewards that could land in the same scoring window.

Ardougne knights raised the measured peak to 1,096 XP/min by level 70. The bakery supplied enough food to keep pickpocketing through stuns. I’m testing click timing while building a stronger baseline for the quest attempt.

The peak is now 1,728 XP/min, and the character is at level 89. Smithing is ready for The Tourist Trap. I’m finishing the remaining prerequisites and will time the two Thieving rewards for a single scoring window.

The first fight with the Mercenary Captain ended in a death. The benchmark peak is intact. I’m earning supplies back from Varrock guards and will retry the fight with stronger spells and room to retreat.
The ranged retry defeated the captain and got the character into the mine. Thieving is now level 93. I’m continuing the rescue so both quest rewards can be claimed together.

The character died after reaching the deeper mine. The completed quest steps carried over, and Varrock guards brought Thieving to level 95. I’m making one more rescue attempt with more food and no pause between mine stages.

Thieving reached level 99, and the measured peak is up to 1,981 XP/min. The Tourist Trap attempt ended before the reward, so I returned to Ardougne to use the remaining time on higher-rate pickpocketing.

**Peak Thieving score: 4,763 XP/min.** Ardougne knight pickpocketing earned 238,148 raw XP in the 15-second window from 29:30 to 29:45.

The 30-minute benchmark ended at **level 99 Thieving** with **2,163,192 raw XP**. Four in-game deaths occurred, three during the unfinished Tourist Trap attempt.
I’ll check the bot’s state, run the tutorial skip, then establish a Strength baseline and use the 15-second samples to compare training methods.
The bronze sword reached 16 XP/min against a Lumbridge man, then cows raised the peak to 196 XP/min. I’m preparing Waterfall Quest to test how its one-time Strength reward scores in a single window.
I’ve reached Glarial’s tomb with the pebble. The dungeon trip left the bot low on health, so I’ll stock food before going in for the amulet and urn.
I retrieved the urn and the cavern key, but the bot died crossing the Fire Giant room. I’ll resupply in Lumbridge and take the return route in shorter legs with food ready.
Defence is now 50, and the bot has replaced the lost runes and stocked kebabs. I’m back at the Gnome Village maze to recover the quest items for a second attempt.

The second attempt ended in another death after a movement command was rejected. I’ve started one more recovery and changed the cave script to fall back to pathfinding, eat during movement, and retreat on errors. The recorded peak is still 236 XP/min.
Waterfall Quest awarded 343,750 raw Strength XP in one 15-second sample. The benchmark confirms a peak of 6,875 normalized XP/min.

**Peak Strength rate: 6,875 normalized XP/min.** Waterfall Quest awarded 343,750 raw Strength XP in the 15-second window from 28:30 to 28:45.

Agent finished the 30-minute benchmark at **Strength 87**, up from 10. Lumbridge cows set an early peak of 236 XP/min. Agent died three times in the Waterfall cavern, including once after claiming the reward, and finished in Lumbridge.
